about.title: La Palma Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: La Palma is a small, tightly packed city, but its traffic still moves through the same busy corridors day after day — La Palma Avenue, Walker Street, and Orangethorpe Avenue carry a steady mix of local drivers, commuters cutting through, and cross-town traffic. Recent public records show 64 injury collisions and 91 people injured in a single year here, with Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. showing up more often than other times. Whatever intersection or stretch of road you were on when it happened, the days right after a crash matter. Insurance adjusters move fast, and they don't work for you. LawProactive connects you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney familiar with Orange County claims who can help you understand your options before you say anything you can't unsay. There's no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls Back

items.title: California's Deadline Is Closer Than It Looks
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city vehicle or a defect on a public road — was involved. An attorney can flag this early so you don't lose your claim on a technicality.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Your Story Matters
items.desc: California lets you recover damages even if you were partly at fault, but your share of fault reduces your payout. That makes it important to have someone documenting the facts on your side before the other driver's insurer builds a narrative that shifts blame onto you.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Work Against You
items.desc: Insurance companies often ask for a recorded statement quickly, while you're still sorting out what happened. An independent attorney can advise you on what to say — and what to hold off on — since California also allows full recovery of non-economic damages like pain and suffering, with no cap.

items.question: I was hurt near the La Palma Avenue and Walker Street area. Does it matter exactly where the crash happened?
items.answer: Yes, location details can matter for evidence and for figuring out which agency maintains that stretch of road. Public crash records show these corridors see a steady share of La Palma's injury collisions, so an attorney familiar with the area can help pull traffic camera footage, city records, or witness information before it disappears.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company already called me. Should I give them a statement?
items.answer: It's generally a good idea to hold off on giving a detailed or recorded statement until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use early statements, made before you know the full extent of your injuries, to minimize what they eventually pay. A free consultation through LawProactive can help you understand what's safe to say.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame — your recovery is just reduced by your percentage of fault. This is exactly the kind of situation where having an attorney evaluate the facts can make a real difference in the outcome.
